title: No coercion (Dignitatis Humanae 2)
hookLine: no one may be forced to act against conscience in religious matters
tomorrow: what do you call a Christian from another church?

lines: A YES SQUEEZED OUT OF YOU.
A SENTENCE FROM THE WRONG BOOK?
FREEDOM, EVEN FOR THE ONE NOT SEEKING.
cards: Pop-ups that won't take no. A salesman with his foot in the door. The friend who keeps bringing it up until you just agree.
Nobody believes a yes that was squeezed out of them. Now here's a sentence that sounds like it wandered in from the wrong book.
A Church document, written by bishops who hold their faith to be true, says the right to religious freedom stays with a person even if that person isn't looking for the truth at all.
Why would a Church protect the freedom of someone ignoring it?

teach.b: The declaration is Dignitatis Humanae, of human dignity, and paragraph two solves the puzzle in three steps. First, what the freedom is.
Everyone, it says, is to be free from coercion: by individuals, by social groups, by any human power at all.

In religious matters, no one is to be forced to act against their conscience, or held back from acting by it, in private or in public, alone or with others, within due limits. Second, what it stands on.
Not a government's permission. Not having the right answers.
It stands on the dignity of the human person, known, the text says, both from God's revealed word and by reason itself. Third, why it matters.
Because people are persons, with reason and free will, they're bound to seek the truth, above all religious truth, and to hold to it once they find it.
And they can't do that unless they're free inside and free from pressure outside. A forced yes isn't a found truth. Now the puzzle solves itself.
If the right came from seeking well, it could be lost by seeking badly.

teach.h: THE FREEDOM STAYS WITH THE PERSON.
teach.b: But it comes from the person.
So the freedom goes wherever the person goes, even down a road the Church thinks is wrong.

how: Catholic teaching since the council holds religious freedom as a right of every person, grounded in human dignity, and the Church speaks up for it in public life.

o: no one may be forced to act against conscience in religion
people never need to follow rules about worship
the Church may not correct anyone about anything

p: force from people, groups or any power
the dignity of the human person
why people are bound to seek truth

s: religious freedom means the Church thinks truth doesn't matter
it says people are bound to seek truth, and can only do it freely.
Dignitatis Humanae grounds religious freedom in human dignity
known from God's revealed word and by reason itself.
the declaration says the right is only for people who are seeking truth
it stays even with those not seeking truth or not holding to it.

games.q: your uncle wants to sign up his grown daughter for a weekend retreat she's said she doesn't want. by Dignitatis Humanae 2, what comes first?
o: the retreat: it's for her own good, so insist.
her freedom: no one forced in religious matters.
the family: parents decide faith for grown kids.
games.why: the declaration says no one is to be forced to act against conscience in religious matters. truth has to be sought freely to be found at all.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone whose beliefs differ from yours, about God or about anything that matters. See them free: thinking, asking, choosing, with no one leaning on them, you included.
Hold that picture with respect while the timer runs.

wordCard.voice: No coercion. Dignitatis Humanae: in religion, no one forced against conscience, because the dignity lives in the person.

orig.note: Latin, 'of human dignity': the declaration's opening words and its name.

carryVoice: Keep this: free to seek, and the freedom goes wherever the person goes. Peace till tomorrow.
